# Plan: plan-carry-forward

Goal: Decide whether sofar_update_plan should carry existing phase and task status forward. The phase-lifecycle final review found that plan_updated is a full replace which appends the caller's payload verbatim (mcp/update-plan.ts has no carry-forward) while the fold rebuilds phases and tasks taking status defaulted to pending (core/fold.ts:1085-1091) — so a replan that omits statuses silently erases progress, and nothing warns, because the fold is doing exactly what it was told. MEASURED 2026-08-13 across 41 records: erasure by OMISSION has never once happened, so this is prevention rather than repair; but erasure by RENAME has happened 7 times, and one of those is why a commit-attribution phase sat in the stale count until phase-lifecycle 4.3 closed it by hand. The live risk is shipping a carry-forward that only half works: every candidate keys on phase name or task id, and none of them rescues a rename. The full-replace contract is what SPEC's forward-compatibility story rests on (task-drop-state D2), so changing it is a Decision, not a patch. Promoted as phase-lifecycle M2.

Progress: 1/9 tasks done (11%)

## Phase 2 — The ruling [pending] — 0/3 done

- [ ] 2.1 DECIDE the mechanism. (a) Merge at the TOOL boundary: update_plan folds current state and carries status forward for matching phase names and task ids unless the caller supplies one — the appended payload stays a COMPLETE plan, so plan_updated's on-disk full-replace contract and replay determinism are both untouched. (b) Merge in the FOLD: preserve status when the payload omits it — the one option that changes how every historical log folds, and therefore the one that can break replay determinism. (c) Detect only: a doctor axis and a warning when a plan_updated drops a resolved status, contract unchanged, loss made visible. (d) Nothing: document the convention. Log the decision citing task-drop-state D2 and phase-lifecycle M2. Note 1.1's result: (a) closes a hole that has never fired.
- [ ] 2.2 DECIDE what protects the closes already written, if 2.1 leaves any window open. 34 phase closes across 16 STILL-ACTIVE records are the concrete thing this initiative exists to stop losing, and they are erasable by the next ordinary replan in any of those records. This is a separate question from the mechanism and must not be assumed answered by it.
- [ ] 2.3 DECIDE what happens across a RENAME — the hole 1.1 found has actually fired, 7 times in 4 records, and the one no candidate mechanism reaches. plan_updated carries no stable phase identity, so a rename and a delete-plus-add are byte-identical in the payload and no merge rule can tell them apart. The options are an id on phases (schema change, and schema lives ONLY in packages/schema/src), an explicit rename affordance, or detection at the boundary. Deciding to do NOTHING is legitimate, but it must be a decision rather than an oversight — shipping (a) alone fixes the hole that never fired and leaves the one that did.
